recipes.name: Steakhouse au Gratin Potatoes
ingredients_raw: salt and black pepper to taste

steps.text: Gather the ingredients. Preheat an oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Grease one 9x13 inch baking pan with butter. Spread potatoes evenly in the pan.
Whisk together heavy cream, milk, garlic, flour, salt, and pepper in a large bowl. Pour cream mixture over the potatoes. Cover with foil.
Bake in the preheated oven for 20 minutes, then remove the foil. Continue baking until the potatoes are easily pierced with a fork, about 40 minutes.
Remove potatoes from the oven and sprinkle Cheddar cheese on top. Return to oven and bake until the cheese is melted, 5 to 10 minutes. Allow to cool for 5 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Steakhouse au Gratin Potatoes
raw_recipe.description: Restaurant-style potatoes au gratin are baked with heavy cream and topped with Cheddar cheese.

review.reviewBody: Hubs made dinner for us tonight and these potatoes were part of it. They were excellent. He used a slightly smaller pan than called for and sliced, rather than cubed the potatoes, but beyond that he strictly stuck to the recipe. We both were really impressed and cleaned these up like nobody's business. So much better, in my view, than the au gratin potatoes with the cheese mixed in with the sauce (the very popular "Creamy Au Gratin Potatoes," also from this site, comes to mind). He didn't measure the cheese, just sprinkled it over the top till it looked just right. The cheese melts and forms a delicious crust over the rich, creamy potatoes. The garlic was just enough to add a little flavor dimension and interest. The fact that it wasn't necessary to cook the sauce on the stove-top first was an added bonus. He served these with a perfectly prepared prime rib roast, steamed broccoli and "Brussels Sprouts with Green Peppers," also from this site. It couldn't have been a better dinner.
These are very tasty. Try boiling the potatoes for about 10 minutes at first, then put together and bake.
Some said this is boring, but I found the cheddar that you use makes or breaks it. For an amazing dish, use a really sharp or old cheddar, really kicks up the taste!

I thought the basic recipe was good. Except I used simply potato fresh hash brown potatoes in the refrigerated aisle near the eggs. I whisked everything in the bowl, just like the original recipe with the exception that I used garlic powder and onion powder instead of fresh garlic. Then I poured the potatoes and a cup of sharp cheddar cheese in the mixture and mixed it up thoroughly and put it in my pan that I had melted one tablespoon of butter in the microwave and smeared it around that way and I baked for 45 minutes and then remove foil and baked another 15 and it was great I loved that I did not have to make a roux on the stove first.

These potatoes were delicious -- very creamy and cheesy. I did make a few adjustments to the recipe -- I added about 1/4 cup diced onion, which I mixed with the potatoes, some onion powder, some seasoned salt (in addition to regular salt), and several drops of hot sauce (Tapatio). Also, used some parmesan cheese in addition to the sharp cheddar. Mixed some of the cheese into the sauce then topped with the remaining cheese at the end as directed by the recipe.

I needed this recipe to use as a starting point. I wanted to fill my large slow cooker so, I sliced thin 10 potatoes, 1 stick of butter, 1 pint of heavy cream, 1/2 cup of milk, 1 cup cheddar cheese, 1/2 cup of parmasan cheese, a pinch of nutmeg, 1 tsp thyme, and a few heavy shakes of garlic powder. I didn't have flour so, I sprinkled the potatoes with 3 tsp of Bisquick then heated the cream, butter, milk, cheeses and pour it over the potatoes. Set the slow cooker to HIgh for 4.5 hours. Crazy Yummy!!!

I made this according to the recipe, but there wasn't much flavor when it came out of the oven. I actually did some post-bake changes - stirred all of it back together (including cheese on top), added a little buttermilk, sour cream, onion powder, garlic powder, re-cheesed the top 2nd time lighter with an extra sharp cheddar, and then broiled it for a few minutes. 2nd time around it actually had some real flavor. Good base, but I think needs some tweaks (we had just been to a local high-end steakhouse and had their au gratin potatoes, so that was our comparison in terms of flavor).

This is a good base recipe - now I just need to get the seasoning right. I used an 8 x 10 casserole dish and sliced four medium-large russet baking potatoes. I had three layers of potatoes with fresh broccoli florets in between. I ended up adding 1 1/2 cups half n half, 1/2 cup heavy cream, and four tablespoons flour, and the consistency of the sauce was perfect. I seasoned the potato layers as another suggested, but it was still a bit bland. Next time I will also add salt and pepper to the sauce mixture. I also added some onion powder and next time I think I will add a little heat, maybe some chipotle powder. I didn't want the cheese to stick to the foil, so once the potatoes were soft, I removed the foil, added the cheese, and baked until the cheese was bubbly. And of course we used sharp cheddar - I never buy anything less than sharp. I would love to try this with some other cheeses as well, maybe add some Manchego. This could easily be customized to pair with the seasonings in your main dish.

So good! Used a smaller square pan vs. the 9x13. Sliced the potatoes vs. chopping up. Used about a tsp of salt and tsp of pepper. Mixed the potatoes up in the mix before placing into the pan and then pouring the rest of the mix over the potatoes. Otherwise, stuck to the instructions provided. Delicious!

O mighty cheddar, here’s a recipe that’s worthy of your sublime flavor ! This recipe is like fireworks for your palate. I liked that it’s so easy to make and who doesn’t like creamy and cheesy potatoes. It goes well with fish and poultry dishes as well, very versatile. I plan to add a larger variety of cheeses the next time I make it, maybe some pecorino or even mozzarella. I’ll also top it with a ton of bacon because well, bacon ! Oh and don’t be scared of how much garlic this recipe needs, you could even add more; potatoes just go so well with garlic.

So much flavor! It was very creamy also. I wish it was a tiny bit more saucy, but I wanted to make sure the potatoes were cooked. Just make sure you put enough salt in it. Potatoes need it. I also added a little bit of onion that I grated on a fine grater (basically a tablespoon of onion pulp) because I like a little onion flavor. It turned out great.
Too much garlic for me. Somewhat overwhelming; covers other flavors. Served with a pan-fried pork steak. Wife loved it.

This is a very tasty dish. I will never buy the box version again. The only change I made, I used sliced potatoes in the can (call me lazy 🤣). Since the potatoes were already cooked , I reduced the cooking time to 25 min. Then put the cheese on top and cooked with the boiler set on low and watched it so it did didn’t burn
Yummy, yum, yum, yum. Served with meatloaf. Easy potatoes dish full of flavor.

I have made several times and everyone likes them. Today I am going to try to add some crunchy fried onions and top with scallions. I won't make too many changes because I know it's a dish my family always eats.

It was a little bland, so I used extra sharp cheddar and sliced potatoes. I was also surprised when the recipe called for one cup of heavy cream and asked for 2% reduced-fat milk? I used whole milk. I will be making this again.
Basically scalloped potatoes with some cheese added. Meh.

This is just a copy of the Pioneer Woman recipe, but with medium cheddar instead of sharp. You should stick to the original, it's much better. My grandparents have made it with sharp cheddar for over 50 years like the Pioneer Woman. It's too bland in this recipe. I added twice the garlic, and some thin sliced green onions, mixed the onion whites in with the rest, then topped with the onion greens with the cheddar for more flavor and a better appearance.
Liked it exactly as directed. Added a bit of Parmesan cheese as an extra.
